runs.content: Thursday's rotation deep-dives Books + Podcasts. Both domains were quiet since the last thinker run (2026-09-23) — no book-summarizer/recommender activity this week, and the only new material anywhere in either domain was today's podcast-recommender batch (4 shows: Darknet Diaries, Money Stuff, High Intensity Health, The Grant Williams Podcast). Found one connection: podcasts/suggestions.md's new Money Stuff (Matt Levine & Katie Greifeld, Bloomberg) recommendation is pitched explicitly for covering 'market structure, weird deal mechanics, regulatory oddities, fraud' — but finance/short-research/ideas-short-selling.md's entire Short Watch List and Pattern Library source exclusively from two channels: Michael Burry's trades and formal published activist short reports (Hindenburg, Muddy Waters, Gotham City). Levine's beat sits structurally earlier in that same pipeline — he's known for catching the exact accounting/deal-mechanics oddities the Pattern Library already names (adjusted-EBITDA abuse, related-party shenanigans, SPAC structuring) in near-real-time commentary, often months before an activist writes a formal report on the same target. Neither page cites the other; the show isn't ingested yet (recommendation only). Concrete next step: if Fred picks it up, add financial journalism (Levine specifically) as a named third source type in ideas-short-selling.md's Pattern Library intro, alongside Burry and the activist-report firms. Checked the open sections for resolution: nothing showed clear signs of being actioned since 2026-09-23.

Wednesday's rotation deep-dives Health + Learning. Both domains are quiet — unchanged since 2026-05-15, no new source material in either since the last Health/Learning-focus run (2026-09-09), and nearly every major gap between them and the rest of the wiki is already logged from prior runs (Health goals stub, my-protocol empty, Ferriss fear-setting, creatine dosing, cognitive-stimulation/games, breathwork/Little Ninja, Seth Godin and Tim Ferriss cross-domain bridges, book-breath cross-link). Deep-read the previously-undived Learning framework pages (empathy-worldview, enrollment, Dave Gray's empathy map, Kevin Kelly's 1,000 True Fans) for a fresh angle instead of re-covering the same ground. Found one: learning/framework-empathy-worldview.md's own 'Applied to Business / Crypto / AI' section gives an explicit diagnostic — when something isn't being adopted, ask what the resister believes/wants/knows that makes non-adoption the rational choice, not why they're being irrational — but it's never been tested against real material. ai-tech/data-ai-enterprise-adoption-economist-2026-06-27.md (an older AI & Tech page, not previously deep-dived) is exactly that material: Natura's CDO's 'I have a Ferrari but I don't have the driver' quote, and the report's own Finding #5 ('the hardest part... is not building the models but rewiring the organisation'), describe stalled AI adoption entirely as a training/ROI-sequencing problem, never naming the possibility that resisting employees hold a rational worldview (job-loss fear, distrust of unaudited AI decisions) — precisely the question the Learning framework was built to ask. The two pages are five weeks apart in creation and have never been linked. Concrete next step: cross-link data-ai-enterprise-adoption-economist-2026-06-27.md's Finding #5 to framework-empathy-worldview.md's belief/want/know diagnostic, both ways.
